title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act establishes clear rules and oversight for the use of artificial intelligence in processing veterans' benefits claims. It aims to ensure that AI systems are transparent, fair, and subject to regular audits so veterans can trust the decisions made about their benefits.

title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act is a proposed law that aims to ban the development, use, or deployment of certain AI systems considered too risky or harmful. It sets out clear rules, enforcement measures, and penalties for companies that create or employ those prohibited AI technologies.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act aims to ensure that artificial intelligence systems used by the U.S. defense sector meet stringent reliability standards and are regularly audited. The law mandates comprehensive reporting of AI performance, safety incidents, and compliance with federal regulations to promote transparency and accountability.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires that all AI systems used by the state of Virginia be clearly documented, including their purpose, data sources, and potential biases. It mandates public disclosure and periodic audits to ensure compliance and to maintain public trust in AI-driven services.

title: To establish a human-centered Federal framework for artificial intelligence in education and the workforce, promote the ethical and responsible teaching and learning of artificial intelligence, provide for equitable access to artificial intelligence-ready workforce development, safeguard student and worker data privacy, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy aims to create a federal, human‑centered framework for using AI in education and the workforce. It focuses on teaching AI responsibly, ensuring equitable access to AI‑ready workforce training, and protecting the privacy of student and worker data.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to create a pilot program that uses artificial intelligence to protect critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It also includes additional measures and responsibilities to support and oversee the program’s implementation.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act would mandate that companies building AI systems put strong security safeguards in place to prevent misuse and protect user data. It would set clear rules, create a certification process, and establish oversight to ensure that all AI products meet high safety and transparency standards.

title: Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act proposes to prohibit the use of artificial intelligence to refuse or deny Medicare claims, ensuring that automated systems cannot be used to withhold coverage or payments. It aims to protect beneficiaries and promote fairness in Medicare benefit decisions.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act would temporarily pause the construction of new AI data centers. This pause is intended to give lawmakers time to evaluate the environmental, economic, and security impacts of large AI infrastructure projects.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to curb unfair pricing practices by AI companies. It would prohibit AI firms from artificially inflating costs and from colluding to set wages, and would impose penalties for violations.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a proposed law designed to protect U.S. AI models from unauthorized copying or distribution. It establishes penalties and safeguards to deter individuals and companies from illegally stealing or exploiting these artificial intelligence creations.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Act sets up a framework for studying how artificial intelligence is used in court proceedings and for creating oversight bodies to ensure those AI tools are fair and transparent. It requires regular reports on AI tools used by judges and lawyers, and establishes standards for accountability, data privacy, and bias mitigation in legal technology.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 establishes guidelines for the responsible use of artificial intelligence by federal agencies, emphasizing transparency, accountability, and protection of privacy. It outlines compliance requirements, risk assessment protocols, and encourages collaboration between government and industry to promote ethical AI deployment.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to prevent artificial intelligence from misleading or tricking users, requiring companies to be clear about when they’re using AI and how it works. It also establishes rules and penalties so that consumers can easily report and be protected against deceptive AI practices.

title: American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act is a proposed U.S. law aimed at establishing national leadership in AI development and ensuring consistent standards across the country. It seeks to coordinate research, set regulatory guidelines, and promote collaboration among federal agencies to maintain a competitive edge in artificial intelligence.

title: Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026 establishes a national framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks associated with the deployment of artificial intelligence systems. It requires federal agencies and private entities to develop risk management plans, conduct impact assessments, and report on compliance to ensure AI technologies are safe, transparent, and aligned with public interest.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The act encourages the use of AI in banking and finance by simplifying regulations, fostering competition, and promoting new services. It also aims to protect consumers and maintain financial stability while enabling innovative AI solutions in the sector.

title: HBCU AI Research Leadership Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The HBCU AI Research Leadership Act aims to give historically black colleges and universities the support they need to become leaders in artificial‑intelligence research. It proposes funding, resources, and partnerships so HBCUs can build strong AI programs and contribute to national innovation.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to equip students and teachers with the knowledge and tools needed to navigate the growing presence of artificial intelligence in society. It will establish nationwide curriculum standards, professional development, and resources to ensure all schools are ready to integrate AI safely and responsibly.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a legal framework designed to guard consumers against misleading or false claims made by AI systems. It mandates that developers disclose when content is AI-generated and sets penalties for deceptive practices in order to ensure transparency and protect user trust.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act establishes legal standards for the responsible development and deployment of artificial intelligence, requiring developers to disclose training data, identify potential biases, and document intended use cases. It also creates oversight mechanisms to protect users, ensuring that AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with public interest.

title: SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Small Business.
summary: The SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act of 2026 requires small businesses to submit regular reports on how they are using artificial intelligence technologies. These reports will help the federal government track AI adoption trends, assess impacts, and inform future policy and support initiatives.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 establishes a comprehensive regulatory framework designed to ensure that artificial intelligence systems are safe, transparent, and ethically aligned. It requires developers to conduct risk assessments, disclose algorithmic decision-making processes, and implement safeguards that protect user privacy and promote accountability across all AI applications.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies that design or use AI systems to conduct detailed impact assessments and disclose how they mitigate bias, privacy, and safety risks. It establishes federal oversight, reporting standards, and penalties for non‑compliance to promote transparency and public accountability in algorithmic decision‑making.

title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 sets federal rules to stop AI systems from infringing on civil rights. It requires companies to be transparent, accountable, and proactive in eliminating bias when creating and using AI.

title: To prohibit the manufacture and conveyance of certain products for children that incorporate an artificial intelligence chatbot, and for other purposes.
action: Sponsor introductory remarks on measure. (CR H3000-3001)
summary: This policy bans the creation and sale of children's products that include an artificial intelligence chatbot. It also sets restrictions on other unspecified uses of such products.

title: To codify Executive Order 14319 (relating to preventing woke AI in the Federal Government).
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The policy aims to turn Executive Order 14319 into enforceable law, focusing on preventing the use of AI systems that could promote or support "woke" ideologies within federal agencies. It establishes guidelines, oversight, and compliance requirements to ensure AI deployment aligns with the government's objectives while avoiding politically or socially driven content.

title: To amend the Public Health Service Act to update quality standards for mammography facilities for the use of AI systems, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy amends the Public Health Service Act to raise the quality standards for mammography facilities that use AI systems. It also includes additional provisions related to the operation and oversight of these AI‑enabled medical imaging services.
